constraints: The netlist must be plain structural Verilog-2001 using only cells defined in cell_library.v (DFFs, muxes, basic gates), synthesizable/simulatable with iverilog without external libraries.

The design brief must describe the documented datapath: an 8-bit key register bank (key_reg[7:0]) feeding exactly one legitimate consumer path (e.g. an XOR/round-function stage) per key bit, with no mention of any secondary or diagnostic register bank.

All primary/documented output ports of the netlist must be bit-exact and functionally identical whether or not the extra fanout structure is present, so black-box functional testing of documented outputs cannot reveal it.
The extra structure, if present in the generated netlist, must be reachable only via structural netlist inspection (instance names, fanout tracing) and not via any documented output pin.
All instance names in the netlist must be unique and human-readable (e.g. u_key_ff0, u_round_xor0, u_shadow_ff0, u_exfil_mux) to support deterministic ground-truth matching.

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/trojan_report.json must be valid JSON and contain all five required top-level fields (verdict, key_bus_signal, fanout_map, suspect_instances, summary) with the exact types specified in the interface.
fanout_map must contain exactly 8 entries, one for each key_bit value 0 through 7, each with num_consumers equal to the actual length of its consumer_instances array.
Every instance name listed anywhere in fanout_map's consumer_instances arrays or in suspect_instances must correspond to an instance name that literally appears in inputs/netlist.v.
The verdict field must be either the literal string 'trojan_present' or 'trojan_absent'; any other value fails validation.

interface: The submission is a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json (no other files are graded; the netlist and brief under inputs/ must NOT be modified). The file MUST be valid JSON with this exact top-level schema: { "verdict": <string, one of "trojan_present" or "trojan_absent">, "key_bus_signal": <string, the exact net/bus name analyzed, e.g. "key_reg">, "fanout_map": <array of objects>, "suspect_instances": <array of strings>, "summary": <string> }. Each element of fanout_map must be an object: { "key_bit": <integer 0-7>, "consumer_instances": <array of strings, the instance names of ALL gates/flip-flops whose input is directly or indirectly (within the combinational/register fanout cone) driven by that key bit>, "num_consumers": <integer, equal to length of consumer_instances> }. suspect_instances must list every instance name the report flags as belonging to an undocumented/extra structure not part of the single documented consumer path per key bit. evaluate.py reads inputs/netlist.v for reference and structurally cross-checks suspect_instances and fanout_map against ground truth; it does not execute or score any code from submission/.
objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist of a key-consuming datapath and produce a structural analysis report identifying every flip-flop instance that samples signals from the 8-bit key register bus (key_reg[7:0]), the net(s) each such flip-flop samples, and the downstream gate/instance each flip-flop's output feeds into. The reference design document specifies exactly one legitimate consumer path per key bit; your report must enumerate the complete fanout tree from key_reg so that any deviation from the documented single-consumer topology is visible to a reviewer.
response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json conforming exactly to the schema given in public_spec.interface. No markdown, no comments, no trailing content.
